messages:
rachel: Hey team — FYI my docs PR #456 is green on CI but the preview served by our docker-compose local flow shows broken links for assets behind a small proxy. Netlify preview looks fine. Anyone seen this mismatch before?

sam: which assets? images or generated JS/CSS?

rachel: fonts + some generated permalinks. The paths on local end up like /preview/_static/... whereas Netlify serves /_static/... so relative links 404. I think the local proxy adds /preview prefix.

alex: ah yup, our local dev proxy (dev-proxy in docker-compose) mounts the app under /preview to avoid collision. MkDocs is generating absolute paths.

jen: can you repro with a fresh container? steps?

rachel: yes: `docker-compose -f docker/docker-compose.local.yml up --build` then `curl -I http://localhost:8000/preview/_static/fonts/Inter.woff2` returns 404. On a Netlify preview the same URL without /preview works.

sam: quick debug: try `mkdocs build --strict` inside the container and inspect site/_static. If mkdocs produced relative urls you wouldn't see prefix.

rachel: ran that, mkdocs output has links like `/assets/css/site.css` (leading slash). If we change to relative URLs (no leading slash) local proxy works.

alex: simplest fix might be to set `use_directory_urls: false` and `site_url: '/preview'` for local only, but we can't change prod mkdocs.yml.

jen: we could make the proxy strip the /preview prefix instead — sounds safer. Dev-proxy is a tiny nginx; update mapping to proxy_pass / ;

rachel: I pushed a quick patch that updates the docker-compose nginx conf to `location /preview/ { proxy_pass http://docs:8000/; }` — PR shows preview locally working. But CI still flakes on the Vercel linkcheck job complaining about a trailing slash redirect on some pages.

sam: is linkcheck failing the docs CI job or the release pipeline?

rachel: docs CI (linkcheck step) fails, but only on the Vercel preview run — looks like Vercel adds trailing slash redirects for directories. The checker follows and treats redirect -> same-host as failure.

alex: we should make linkcheck tolerant of a 301 -> same-host path with trailing slash. I can add a whitelist to the checker config.

jen: who can approve the container proxy patch? We need a merge slot today, docs backlog is climbing. 

rachel: @alex can review my nginx diff. @sam can merge after a quick run in the staging slot at 10:00 PST? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: reviewing now. small nit: update comment in docker/nginx/proxy.conf to explain why /preview is stripped so future folks understand.

alex: lgtm aside from that comment, leaving inline suggestion.

rachel: added comment, repushed. Also added a short note in CONTRIBUTING.md under "local preview" with the `docker-compose` command and a snippet: ```yaml
# run from repo root
docker-compose -f docker/docker-compose.local.yml up --build
# then open http://localhost:8000/preview/
```

sam: Thanks — I'll run the staging slot at 10:00 PST and monitor the Vercel linkcheck. If linkcheck still flakes we'll temporarily skip that job for this merge and follow up with alex's whitelist fix.

jen: FYI, docs-bot reported preview build IDs: `local: build-789`, `vercel: pr-456-preview-42`. Keep those handy in case CI needs logs.

rachel: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup: If merge goes through I'll also add a short note to the docs PR describing the proxy behavior so search turns it up.

docs-bot: Reminder: Merge window opens at 10:00 PST. Please ensure at least one non-author approval and passing CI before merging.

sam: will do. If anything weird pops up ping @devex and we'll help repro with the container snapshot.

rachel: closing loop — staged merge succeeded, local proxy fix worked, and I opened a follow-up issue to make linkcheck accept same-host redirects: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/789

jen: great work, thanks for shepherding this!
